blocks.text: Vascular disorders affect the blood vessels of the brain and spinal cord; examples are stroke and cerebral venous thrombosis.

blocks.caption: Stroke
rows: damage to brain cells when the blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted by a blocked or ruptured vessel
high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, family history of stroke

depend on the area affected: paralysis on the side opposite the cerebral infarction (dead tissue); aphasia (inability to express in words); sudden trouble seeing or walking; dizziness, loss of balance; severe headache

as soon as possible: medicines (blood thinners, clot-dissolving drugs, drugs for high blood pressure); surgery to remove a clot or repair a burst vessel; rehabilitation to recover physical and mental function

items: Ischaemic stroke: the brain's blood vessels become narrowed or blocked.
Haemorrhagic stroke: a blood vessel in the brain leaks or ruptures.
Transient ischaemic attack (mini-stroke): a temporary drop in blood supply to part of the brain, which may last as little as five minutes.

blocks.alt: A brain with two affected areas, a blue one at the front and a red one at the back. Each is enlarged as a cut-open artery: on the left a clot blocks the artery (Blockage); on the right blood escapes through a tear in the artery wall (Rupture). Both arteries have fatty deposits on their walls.
